step1_analysis.description: This is a common-source, common-gate (cascode) amplifier core typically used in RF LNAs. The common-source transistor (XM2) provides transconductance, while the common-gate transistor (XM1) provides isolation, increases output impedance, and mitigates the Miller effect to achieve high frequency operation.

paper_reference.title: A 5.2-GHz LNA in 0.35-m CMOS Utilizing Inter-Stage Series Resonance and Optimizing the Substrate Resistance

voltage_gain.description: Voltage gain of the amplifier at the operating frequency (5.2 GHz)

sky130_expected.calculation: Gain ≈ gm * Rload. For W=50u, Id ≈ 5mA, gm ≈ 50mS. With a 500 ohm tuned load, intrinsic gain is ~25 V/V (28 dB). Accounting for parasitics and source matching, expect 15-20 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Sky130 0.15um has higher gm/Id than 0.35um, allowing similar or better gain at lower supply voltages, heavily dependent on the LC tank Q-factor.

noise_figure.description: Noise Figure (NF) at 5.2 GHz, representing the degradation of SNR

sky130_expected.calculation: NF = 10 * log10(inoise_spectrum / (4*k*T*Rsrc)). Dominated by the common-source transistor's channel noise.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The shorter channel length of Sky130 (0.15um vs 0.35um) provides a higher fT, which generally translates to a lower minimum noise figure (NFmin).

dc_power.description: Total DC power consumption from the supply

sky130_expected.calculation: Pdc = VDD * Id. For a typical LNA bias of 5mA at 1.8V, Pdc = 9 mW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Scaled down from the 3.3V supply used in the 0.35um paper to the 1.8V standard supply of Sky130.

peak_frequency.description: Frequency at which the voltage gain reaches its maximum

sky130_expected.calculation: f_peak = 1 / (2 * pi * sqrt(L * C_total)). With L=1nH and C=0.5pF + transistor parasitics, it tunes near 5.2 GHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined by the LC tank components added in the testbench to replicate the LNA's tuned load.

sky130_expected.calculation: Requires two-tone transient analysis and FFT. Typically 5-15 dBm for LNAs.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends on bias current, overdrive voltage, and load impedance.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC power, AC voltage gain, peak frequency, Noise Figure, and transient swing of the cascode LNA core.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Cascode LNA Core Testbench
.lib "sky130_fd_pr/models/sky130.lib.spice" tt

* Upsized W and L for RF LNA operation
.param W_xm1=50u L_xm1=0.15u
.param W_xm2=50u L_xm2=0.15u

* DUT
* Note: XM1 gate was changed from GND to VB to allow proper cascode biasing.
XM1 N7 VB N2 N2 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 N2 LABEL_NET_0 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}

* Biasing and Supply
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VVB VB 0 1.8

* Input Source (50 ohm source resistance, DC bias 0.9V, AC 1V, Transient 10mV peak at 5.2GHz)
V_in N_src 0 dc 0.9 ac 1 sin(0.9 0.01 5.2G)
R_src N_src LABEL_NET_0 50

* Tuned Load (Resonates near 5.2 GHz)
L1 VDD N7 1n
C1 N7 0 0.5p
R1 N7 VDD 500

.control
* 1. DC Analysis
op
let idc = -i(VVDD)
let power = idc * 1.8
print idc power

* 2. AC Analysis
ac dec 100 1G 10G
let gain_db = vdb(N7)
meas ac gain_5g find gain_db at=5.2G
meas ac max_gain max gain_db
meas ac peak_freq when gain_db=max_gain

* 3. Noise Analysis
* Calculates input-referred noise spectrum and derives Noise Figure (NF)
noise v(N7) V_in dec 50 1G 10G
setplot noise1
meas noise inoise_5g find inoise_spectrum at=5.2G
* Thermal noise of 50 ohm resistor at 300K is 4*k*T*R = 8.28e-19 V^2/Hz
let nf_db = 10 * log10(inoise_5g / 8.28e-19)
print nf_db

* 4. Transient Analysis
* 5.2 GHz period is ~192ps. Simulate for 1ns, measure last 0.5ns.
tran 2p 1n
meas tran vout_max max v(N7) from=0.5n to=1n
meas tran vout_min min v(N7) from=0.5n to=1n
let vout_pp = vout_max - vout_min
* Input is 20mV peak-to-peak
let gain_v_v = vout_pp / 0.02
print vout_pp gain_v_v

quit
.endc
.end
